summary: Red Planet Outpost is a browser game for kids aged 7–12 that teaches one hard truth about living on Mars: there is never enough power for everything. Players command a solar-powered outpost for 10 sols, sharing a small power budget between Life Support, Shielding, Comms and Science. Solar storms come from real NASA DONKI flare and solar-particle records, including the September 2017 and May 2024 events that reached Mars, or from the live Sun today. Protecting the crew means doing less science, and kids learn that trade-off by making it. Every number in the game is traced to a NASA source, and the game says plainly where it scales reality to make choices matter. It needs no account, no ads and no backend.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Each sol, the player places a few solar power cells into four systems. Life Support keeps the crew alive. Shielding blocks storm radiation for the crew inside. Comms brings tomorrow's space-weather forecast from Earth. Science sends the rover out to collect samples. The mission goal is 22 samples without going over the radiation dose limit. Working outside during a storm adds a lot of dose that shielding cannot block, so the winning habit is the real one astronauts follow: watch the forecast, cancel outside work on storm days, and shelter.

Three mission types:

- Real Storm Replay: September 2017 or May 2024, built from NASA DONKI solar flare (FLR) and solar energetic particle (SEP) records.

- Today's Sun: live DONKI data from the last 10 days.

- Random: seeded practice missions.

After the mission, a debrief shows the player's key decisions and "Real NASA Science" cards on bones, muscles, body clocks and radiation in space, drawn from NASA OSDR studies. A "Science Behind This" page lists each real value, the value the game uses, and why they differ. A Teacher page supports classroom use.

HOW IT WORKS

- Flare class C/M/X is mapped to a small, medium or big storm. A linked, measured SEP event becomes a radiation spike.

- The simulation is pure and deterministic (state + choices + seed -> new state), so every mission can be reproduced and tested.

- Live data falls back in a set order: CCMC DONKI, then api.nasa.gov/DONKI, then the last live download, then a bundled snapshot. Saved data is always labelled ARCHIVED, never LIVE.

- The game was balance-tested with 1,000 seeded missions per strategy. No fixed strategy wins more than 60% of runs, and a player who reacts to warnings beats the best fixed plan by 15+ points. Thinking ahead pays off, and no single trick does.

HONESTY ABOUT LIMITS

During the hackathon, DONKI's flare-list endpoint returned errors, so replay flares come from DONKI flare notifications and are complete only for class M5.0 and above. Particle events are complete. Storm doses are scaled above real Mars-surface values so choices matter in 10 turns. The game states both of these to players.

BENEFITS AND GOALS

It turns real space-weather data into a decision a child can feel: shielding the crew means less science today. It works offline after loading, has no tracking, and runs on any tablet or laptop browser.

TOOLS

TypeScript, Preact, Vite, Vitest, tsx; Lexend and Unbounded fonts (Fontsource); Phosphor icons; layered SVG animation that respects reduced-motion settings; static hosting on GitHub Pages.

Source code: https://github.com/thesweetmouther/spynal-red-planet-outpost
